# ghost_team_repository (Resource)

Gives a team a role on a repository owned by the team's organization. Every member of the team gets the role on the repository. Teams can't be created with an API token, so the team must already exist: look it up with the `ghost_team` or `ghost_organization_teams` data source, or name it with `team_slug`. You must be an admin of the repository. Repositories owned by a user can't be shared with teams.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "ghost_repository" "example" {
  owner = "my-org"
  name  = "example"
}

data "ghost_team" "core" {
  organization = "my-org"
  slug         = "core"
}

# Give every member of the team write access to the repository.
resource "ghost_team_repository" "core" {
  repository = ghost_repository.example.full_name
  team_id    = data.ghost_team.core.id
  role       = "write"

  # Recreate the access if the repository is replaced, which drops it.
  lifecycle {
    replace_triggered_by = [ghost_repository.example.repo_id]
  }
}

# Or name the team by its slug, without a data source.
resource "ghost_team_repository" "docs" {
  repository = ghost_repository.example.full_name
  team_slug  = "docs"
  role       = "triage"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `repository` (String) The repository's full name, `organization/slug`, e.g. `ghost_repository.example.full_name`. The repository must belong to the team's organization. Renaming the repository updates this in place; pointing it at a different repository forces a new resource.
- `role` (String) The role every member of the team gets on the repository: `read`, `triage`, `write`, `maintain` or `admin`. Changing it updates the resource in place.

### Optional

- `team_id` (String) The team's ID, e.g. `data.ghost_team.example.id`. It never changes, even if the team is renamed. Exactly one of `team_id` and `team_slug` must be set; when `team_slug` is set, this is the ID it names. Changing the team forces a new resource.
- `team_slug` (String) The team's slug, matched case-insensitively. Exactly one of `team_id` and `team_slug` must be set; when `team_id` is set, this is the team's current slug. A slug changes when the team is renamed, so prefer `team_id` where you can. Changing it to another team's slug forces a new resource; changing it to the same team's new slug doesn't.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The repository's full name and the team ID, `owner/slug:team_id`.
- `repository_id` (Number) The numeric ID of `repository`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Team access is imported by the repository's full name and the team's ID or
# slug, "owner/slug:team".
terraform import ghost_team_repository.core my-org/example:DG4eRcoHLcE1RfixZDetBcBzEQBBYIbb
terraform import ghost_team_repository.docs my-org/example:docs
```
